column1: # Which flash attention route encodes an op.
# How the rows are used: flash-attn/gen-routes.cmake compiles them in when CMake configures (routes-table.h). The router
# (flash-attn/router.cpp) walks the rows in order and takes the first one whose cells all match. The Intel tiled route may
# decline (no kernel for the head size), and the walk goes on. No row matches = the op is not taken here. No file is read at run time.
# To add a route: write flash-attn/route-<name>.cpp, add its name to the generator and the router, then add its row.
# In every condition column, any = the column does not restrict the row.
# A line that is exactly [name] starts a section; the next row is that section's header and is required as written: the
# generators read the cells by position.
# [routes]: which route encodes an op (the rows described above).
# Columns
#   order: the place in the walk, counting up from 1 with no gap.
#   route: intel-tiled | scalar | matrix | vec. The encoder the row selects.
#   file: the source file of that encoder, for the reader of this table. The code does not read this cell.
#   needs_matrix: the card has simdgroup matrices: yes | no | any.
#   vendor: intel | not-intel | any.
#   width: the card's simd width: 32 | not-32 | any.
#   batch: small (under 20 queries and a head size that is a multiple of 32) | large | any.
#   kv: the K and V types: same | differ | any.
#   fp8: K is f8_e4m3: yes | no | any.
#   head: the head size the route has a kernel for: a number | any.
#   note: why the row exists or what limits it. Free text, no tab. The code does not read this cell.
# [launch]: the launch numbers of a route. flash-attn/gen-routes.cmake compiles the rows in (fa-launch-table.h);
# fa_launch_pick (flash-attn/launch.cpp) gives the numbers of one route on the card it runs on, in this order, a later
# row's cell that is not - replacing the earlier value: the route's default row (card any, wave any; exactly one, before
# the route's other rows, writing every cell the route reads), the route's row of the card's wave (card any, wave a
# number), the card's own row (card = its Metal device name, wave = the wave it reports).
# workgroups and small_queries hold for every card (the workspace of an op is sized before the card is known,
# flash-attn/sizes.cpp), so only a default row writes them. What a kernel fixes stays in code: queries and cache values
# per simdgroup of the vec and matrix kernels, the Intel tiled kernel's 128 threads and tile of 32.
# The generator holds the values each cell takes (the bound_ lines of flash-attn/gen-routes.cmake) and refuses a value
# outside them: scalar simdgroups 1 to 8; vec simdgroups 1, 2 or 4, workgroups 32, small_queries 1 to 32; matrix
# simdgroups and wide_simdgroups 4 or 8; prepass threads 32. To widen one, read the consumer named beside its line first.
# To change a number for a card: measure FLASH_ATTN_EXT on the card with and without it, same output, and add the card's row.
#   launch_route: scalar | vec | matrix | prepass (the pad and block pre-pass). Each route reads only its own cells; the others are -.
#   card: [launch]: any | the card's name as Metal reports it.
#   wave: [launch]: any | the threads of one wave the card reports. A card's row writes a number.
#   simdgroups: scalar: simdgroups per query. vec: the most simdgroups per threadgroup (they double from 1 while the cache is longer than the launch covers). matrix: simdgroups per threadgroup.
#   wide_simdgroups: matrix: simdgroups per threadgroup from a head size of wide_head. - on the other routes.
#   wide_head: matrix: the head size from which wide_simdgroups apply. - on the other routes.
#   workgroups: vec: the parts the cache is split into; the launch, the merge stage and the workspace size read it. - on the other routes.
#   small_queries: vec: an op of fewer queries than this (and a head size that is a multiple of 32) is a small batch (the batch column of [routes]). - on the other routes.
#   threads: prepass: threads per threadgroup. - on the other routes.
#   evidence: where each written cell comes from. Free text, no tab.
[routes]
order
